messages:
eve.customer: Our hosted inference endpoint started returning 502s and extreme first-byte latency this morning after a cert rotation. Customers in eu-west1 see it most. Curl shows TLS timeout then connection reset. Repro (from our VM):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'
*   Trying 34.120.10.11...
* Connected to api.redwood.example (34.120.10.11) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLS handshake timeout
* Connection reset by peer
```
Request id header missing in responses. Any ideas?

alice.support: Sorry you're hitting this — thanks for the logs. Can you paste the exact request id if you have one from your SDK? Also which model/route and whether you used streaming?

eve.customer: No request id in response. We call the text-generation route (gpt-open-8k) non-streaming. Happens on warm and cold starts. Happens across a handful of orgs in our account.

ben.platform: Noted. I see a cert rotation deployed at ~1745677200 from our deploy-bot. Will check rollout groups. @deploy-bot can you paste the rotation job id and whether any hosts failed health checks?

deploy-bot: cert-rotation job=rot-2024-11-03-18-00 status=completed rollout_groups=all regions=global failed_hosts=0 health_failures=0

carlos-ingest: Quick note: control-plane logs show repeated TCP_RST from a subset of egress NATs in eu-west1 for ports 443 -> 59224 around the same time window. Not seeing errors in other regions.

alice.support: Two likely culprits: (1) intermediate resolver returning stale CNAMEs during the rotation causing SNI mismatch on the gateway, or (2) upstream egress NAT overload leading to truncated TLS handshakes. Can you run a dns dig + trace from the customer's VM and share? Example: `dig +trace api.redwood.example`

eve.customer: Ran trace, attaching excerpt:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> +trace api.redwood.example
.		IN	A
api.redwood.example.  60 IN CNAME lb-42.prod.redwood.example.
lb-42.prod.redwood.example. 300 IN A 34.120.10.11
;; Received 192.0.2.53#53(192.0.2.53) from 192.0.2.1#53(192.0.2.1) in 10 ms
```
But sometimes the dig returns a different A (34.120.11.22) and then curl fails.

ben.platform: That points at DNS churn / inconsistent resolving across resolver cluster. During cert rotation our TLS stack validates SNI+cert chain; if client resolves to an instance that hasn't finished loading the new cert or has a different IP->SNI mapping, handshake can drop. We had a partial rollout window.

alice.support: For short-term mitigation: (a) try forcing your client to a known-good resolver (e.g., 8.8.8.8) to test if your resolver cache is serving stale glue, (b) set SDK retry to 3 with jitter, (c) enable fallback to the regional host header we can share.

ben.platform: We're also going to push a hotfix to the rollout: ensure cert and SNI mapping update are applied atomically on the load-balancer side to avoid split-horizon DNS windows. Also increasing egress NAT pool size for eu-west1 to prevent transient RSTs while the rollout completes.

carlos-ingest: Logged a support ticket to infra: INFRA-6721. I'll attach tcpdump snippet request so we can correlate client->gateway handshake packets. Example tcpdump we need from your VM: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 34.120.10.11 and port 443 -w redwood-conn.pcap`

eve.customer: Will run tcpdump and try 8.8.8.8. Also repro steps: 1) cold VM, 2) `curl` loop 50x parallel, 3) observe ~20% TLS handshake failures, 4) switch resolvers -> failures drop to <1%.

alice.support: Perfect repro — that strongly implicates resolver variance. We'll keep you patched in the INFRA ticket. For now, as a bandaid you can: set DNS to 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1, or pin the working IP in your hosts file for short-term.

ben.platform: Follow-ups: infra will (1) coordinate a tighter cert rollout with atomic SNI update, (2) increase NAT pool, (3) add a short-lived DNS TTL smoothing rule during cert rotations to avoid split-caches.

eve.customer: Thanks all — running tcpdump now and will post the pcap link. Really appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
